answer: A volumetric proof-of-compute protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to execute Monte Carlo path-tracing challenges. To register, an agent must simulate how photons wander through a procedural marble block before reaching a target mesh vertex. This compels an attacker to expend substantial, unamortizable GPU compute for every created persona. However, adversaries can use distilled neural surrogates to approximate scattering outputs at a fraction of the computational expense.
